A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same music-moment grounding research, with matching benchmark totals and splits despite renamed tasks, datasets and methods. Text, equations, tables and figures are readable, including v1 Appendix A. v2 ends after its references without an appendix.

before.justification: v1 reports original ReaL evaluations, ablations, an annotation-quality user study and qualitative localization results, including appendix examples.

after.justification: v2 reports original MaDe and baseline evaluations, ablations, inference timings and a human preference study in Tables 4–7 and Figure 4.

M1.justification: The separately trained retrieval and Music-DETR stages of ReaL are replaced by jointly trained MaDe. v2 adds X-Pool matching, replaces cross-attention fusion with concatenation and self-attention, and uses a single-query decoder. v1's moment-classification and auxiliary moment-alignment components disappear; matching and localization losses are jointly optimized.

E1.justification: v1 trains and evaluates retrieval on HIMV-138k in addition to Ad-Moment; v2 removes this music-video benchmark and evaluates only MGSV-EC. Ad-Moment and MGSV-EC have identical reported corpus and split statistics. SmG and MsG correspond to v1's localization and corpus-retrieval tasks, so their renaming does not add coverage.

E2.justification: v1's sliding-window and highlight-detection comparators disappear from the main grounding comparisons. v2 Table 4 evaluates Moment-DETR, QD-DETR, TR-DETR, EaTR, UVCOM, three CA-removed variants, MVPt/MVPt+, their composite solution and CONQUER. MVPt changes from a cited cross-dataset result in v1 to an implemented comparator on the retained benchmark.

E3.justification: The moment-recall IoU threshold changes from 0.5 to 0.7, R25 is dropped, and v2 specifies one moment per ranked track. Separate 100/80-epoch AdamW training becomes joint 100-epoch Adam training; frame resizing changes from 224 to 256 pixels. Annotation provenance changes from waveform matching to editing logs, although whether annotations were recomputed is unresolved.

E4.justification: v2 replaces the shortcut, alignment-loss and stride analyses with broader tests of X-Pool, fusion, query initialization/count, width prediction and decoder depth, plus efficiency analysis. The video-initialization question is retained and expanded. v1's annotation audit, duration-fit plot and appendix case studies disappear; v2 adds a blinded output-preference study.

E5.justification: Both retain dataset duration means and standard deviations and report model performance without training-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Changed human-study sample sizes and preference percentages do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: v1 Tables 4–5 report ReaL mIoU 0.602 and R100 18.55 at IoU threshold 0.5. v2 Table 4 reports MaDe mIoU 0.722 and MoR100 30.7 at threshold 0.7, alongside extensive new comparator and ablation results. Figure 4 adds preferences of 39.4% for MaDe versus 28.0% for the composite. These are different-model/protocol results, not established same-setting gains.

T1.justification: The mathematical matching-score definition changes: v2 Equation (3) sums cosine similarities from mean-pooled and X-Pool embeddings, replacing v1's single-similarity formulation. This is a limited mathematical reformulation accompanying the method revision; neither version develops theorems, proofs or theoretical guarantees.

C1.justification: The underlying task remains music-moment selection for short videos, renamed MGSV. However, the main contribution changes from a weakly supervised timestamp pipeline and two-stage ReaL to an editing-log benchmark and unified MaDe matching/detection network. v2 also foregrounds systematic adaptation of existing grounding models as a contribution.

C2.justification: The explanation shifts from music shortcuts, moment alignment and masking-based duration learning to partial relevance handled by X-Pool and benefits from avoiding CA-based multimodal fusion. v2 attributes CA fusion's weakness to overfitting and explicitly acknowledges that the underlying difference between music grounding and text-video grounding remains unexplained.

D1.justification: v2 adds the exact CLIP variant, PyTorch version, attention heads, dropout, positional encoding, initialization and module-level parameter/timing information, and reports different GPU hardware. It omits v1's explicit audio sampling, window/stride and padding recipe. v1's project link is replaced by a future code/data-release statement, without establishing actual availability.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially recentered on DETR-style grounding architectures and their suitability for music, including a new structural comparison in Table 1. New references include EaTR, TR-DETR, UVCOM, X-Pool and MuseChat. Much of v1's metadata-based retrieval, source-separation and broader localization discussion is removed.

P1.justification: The title, terminology, abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion are extensively rewritten. Dataset evaluation protocols move into Section 3, methods are organized around the unified network and its training, and evaluation is divided by grounding mode. v1's separate appendix is removed.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the opening schematic with prominent visual examples and replaces separate retrieval/localization diagrams with a unified MaDe diagram. Dataset graphics are substantially recomposed, comparison results are consolidated with parameter counts, and architecture, protocol, ablation and timing tables are added. v1's duration plot and appendix pipeline/case-study figures are not retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens the central evidence: v1 relies on simple grounding baselines and a separate retrieval comparison across mismatched datasets, while v2 provides stronger baselines under controlled conditions, component-specific ablations and blinded human preferences. Clearer organization also improves assessability. These gains outweigh the loss of HIMV coverage and appendix analyses, although the unexplained annotation-provenance change and omitted preprocessing details remain reproducibility weaknesses.
